authors: Z. Bern, S. Davies, T. Dennen, A.V. Smirnov, V.A. Smirnov
title: Ultraviolet properties of N=4 supergravity at four loops
claim: Pure N=4 supergravity diverges at four loops in D=4 (four-point amplitude); the form of the divergence suggests it is due to the rigid U(1) duality-symmetry anomaly.
scheme: Integrand from colour-kinematics duality (double copy of N=4 SYM with pure YM); UV divergence extracted with standard methods (DR implied; scheme not named in the abstract).
symmetry_argument: Double copy; no statement on regulator symmetry. Divergence linked (as a suggestion) to the U(1) anomaly.

proved: Explicit nonzero four-loop UV divergence in this computational setup.
assumed: Interpretation via the U(1) anomaly is a suggestion, not derived.

evidence: Abstract: first UV divergence in a pure ungauged 4d supergravity; anomaly interpretation suggested.
red_flags: Later work (S1d.10_BPR2017) showed anomalous one-loop amplitudes and evanescent terms can be removed by a finite local counterterm and that the four-loop divergence was computed without it; the physical status of the divergence depends on this DR/evanescent/anomaly interplay.
cross_checks: Re-examination called for in 1712.03928 (S1d.10_BPR2017); evanescent/anomaly link 1706.01486.
notes: Included because it is the cleanest example where a DR UV result is entangled with an anomaly and evanescent operators.
